notes: Scaffold metrics for civic power, corruption resistance, and responsiveness. Replace placeholders with best-guess estimates + logic + ranges.

participation_index.assumption: Participation remains suppressed by cynicism, barriers, and low trust.
participation_index.mechanism: Complex systems and money influence reduce perceived impact.
participation_index.rationale: People disengage when outcomes feel predetermined.

corruption_visibility_index.assumption: Transparency remains partial; procurement opacity persists.
corruption_visibility_index.mechanism: Lobbying and contracting information remains hard to audit.

money_influence_index.assumption: High dependence on donor class continues.
money_influence_index.mechanism: Campaign finance structures reward concentrated wealth.
money_influence_index.rationale: Money buys access when systems allow it.

participation_index.assumption: Local-first power and simplified civic systems increase participation.
participation_index.mechanism: Decisions become closer to daily life and more visible.
participation_index.rationale: People engage when their voice has clear impact.

corruption_visibility_index.assumption: Audit-by-default laws and machine-readable budgets/contract logs.
corruption_visibility_index.mechanism: Transparency becomes a system requirement, not optional.
corruption_visibility_index.rationale: Visibility deters corruption and enables citizen oversight.

money_influence_index.assumption: Public financing and contribution-based systems de-emphasize donor control.
money_influence_index.mechanism: Lower dependence on private fundraising reduces capture.
money_influence_index.rationale: When elections don’t require donor pipelines, money loses leverage.
